model_annotations.Bulgarian: Figure 4 illustrates the mean absolute values of hidden states before and after the application of a gating mechanism, across different network layers, with the stated intent to compare baseline and post-gating behavior. The horizontal axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to 25, with major tick marks and labels at intervals of 5 (0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25), indicating a linear scale representing the depth of the neural network. The vertical axis, labeled “Abs. Mean,” ranges from 0 to 1.0, with tick marks and labels at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, and 1.0, representing the average absolute magnitude of the hidden state activations. Three distinct lines are plotted: a solid green line labeled “Hidden state mean before gate, avg 0.71,” which remains relatively flat and close to 0.7 across all layers; a dashed green line labeled “Hidden state mean after gate, avg 0.05,” which stays near zero throughout the layer range; and a dotted green line labeled “Hidden state mean of baseline, avg 0.04,” which also remains near zero and closely tracks the post-gating line. The visual comparison shows that the pre-gating values are substantially higher than both the post-gating and baseline values, which are nearly identical across all layers.
